en.title: Maximum Distinct Items Owned Within Budget
en.description:
A store sells items numbered 1 to n, and item i costs i. You already own the items in arr; find the total number of distinct items you own after buying within budget k. Items you already own count even if they are outside the store's range, and duplicate numbers count only once.

The standard input/output format and examples were compiled by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m k, and the second line contains the m numbers of owned items. 1≤n≤10^6, 1≤m≤10^5, 1≤k≤10^9, 1≤arr[i]≤10^6.
en.explanation: The examples give 5, 2 and 2 respectively. In the first example the owned item 6 still counts, and 1, 2 and 4 are newly bought.
hints: Deduplicate the owned numbers, then go from 1 to n buying each item you do not own while you can afford it; stop when you cannot.
